evidence_policy: Author names and commit messages are provenance only. A preference needs an explicit instruction or a deliberate corrective diff retained by later source edits.

preferences.rule: Keep the five-chapter persistent SMP campaign and do not restore retired chapters, deleted capstones, or a Neutral progression chapter.
preferences.before: Historical designs used larger seasonal graphs, breadth gates, capstones, and a third civic progression lane.
preferences.after: The current design retains five chapters with Neutral as a protected opt-out.

preferences.rule: Preserve explicitly protected Chapter 4 coordinates and the established horseshoe; preserve Chapter 5 catalogue departments and center-weighted information nodes.
preferences.before: Generic graph layouts and orthogonal routing obscured the deliberate arrangement.
preferences.after: Source-faithful layout remains authoritative; diagnostic routing is optional and labeled.

preferences.rule: Use real workstations, apparatus, recipes, outputs, and bounded manual attestations to teach a coherent mechanic.
preferences.before: Generic block stockpiles and lore checklists stood in for usable gameplay.
preferences.after: Chapter 4 commissions and specialties establish a service, then teach its later workflow.

preferences.rule: Generous common-material building palettes are approved when purchased with currency; that approval does not restore large free construction rewards.
preferences.before: Older balance notes treated large material bundles as generally prohibited.
preferences.after: Bulk common materials belong in finite paid Market palettes, while one-time faction rewards remain thematic and bounded.

preferences.rule: A paid Market redemption is one shared payment and one shared reward entitlement per FTB Team; claim scope must follow installed FTB Quests claim keys.
preferences.before: The earlier source and docs described paid rewards as personal and treated team_reward=false as sufficient scope control.
preferences.after: Paid purchases are modeled as shared entitlements; the weekly Rumour Ledger remains separately team-scoped and slow.
preferences.scope: FTB Quests payment and claim behavior

preferences.rule: Use 180 seconds for building purchases and 300 seconds for progression or utility purchases; keep recurring currency issuance on its separately approved seven-day schedule.
preferences.before: A weekly purchase-board proposal conflated purchase restocking with currency issuance.
preferences.after: Purchase delay and faucet cadence are documented and audited as separate controls.

preferences.rule: Preserve existing Chapter 5 crate, task, quest, and unchanged reward IDs; record any genuine replacement mapping.
preferences.after: The four preserved crates remain 7A11C0DF00500011 through 00014 with task IDs ending 00021 through 00024.

preferences.rule: Resolve every non-vanilla item from the pinned artifact/catalogue and distinguish registry, recipe, obtainability, and runtime evidence.
preferences.before: Display-name guesses and unrelated JAR matches entered quest tasks and rewards.
preferences.after: The current workflow records exact artifact evidence and leaves runtime resolution explicitly pending.

preferences.rule: Reconcile live SNBT before generation and preserve unrelated chapter fields, manual edits, coordinates, and stable IDs.
preferences.before: A stale whole-campaign generator could erase richer manual content.
preferences.after: Reviewed overlays, hash ledgers, temporary generation, and semantic --check protect retained edits.

preferences.rule: Do not infer IDs from names, stale appendices, or author identity; stop at an explicit unresolved evidence state.
preferences.before: Legacy appendix IDs and guessed decorative names were presented as current.
preferences.after: The report and docs label unresolved registry/recipe/runtime checks instead of claiming completion.

preferences.rule: Record reversals explicitly: exact old completionism parity, weekly purchase issuance, and automatic bulk claim behavior are not current requirements.
preferences.before: Historical validators and docs expected breadth gates, capstones, exact parity, or weekly purchase boards.
preferences.after: The current brief prioritizes preserved graph structure, shared paid stock, and separate runtime acceptance tests.
